what: spec_context.json under bot v55 (2026-10-14). Everything in spec_context.json holds, except where the rules below say otherwise. The labels of 'orders' are spec_v55.json's: three new intents (GET_IN, GET_OUT, REPEAT), a negated order is WAIT, waiting at a place is HOLD_POSITION, fetching an item (ammo, a weapon, health) and going to a car are MOVE_TO.
rules: 1b. Rule 1 changes for repeats: a line that only asks for the last thing again ('try again', 'again', 'do that again', 'one more time', 'once more', 'more', 'same again') is written back AS IT IS; its order is REPEAT. The game knows what was done and what failed, and repeats the right part. An order said again with its own verb is that order ('frag it again' -> 'frag it again', FRAG; with a place left out, rule 5 fills it in).

4b. A fragment that names a place with a pointing word ('to this wall', 'at that window', 'over there', 'on my pin', 'that one') right after an order completes that order and KEEPS the pointing word: before: ['start shooting']; line: 'to this wall' -> 'Shoot at this wall.'. before: ['watch the stairs']; line: 'no, that window' -> 'Watch that window.'. Rule 8 still holds for a line that is a whole order by itself ('go there' stays 'go there').

6b. An answer to the bot's 'Which ...?' that points somewhere else ('on my pin', 'that one over there', 'here') is the order the bot asked about, at that place, with the pointing words kept: before: ['Shoot this window.']; bot: 'Which window? The one on the left, 10 m?'; line: 'on my pin' -> 'Shoot at my pin.'. bot: 'Which door?'; line: 'the one by my pin' -> 'Breach the door by my pin.'.

7b. A negated order is not rewritten: 'don't', 'don't do that', 'no, don't go there', 'don't jump down' stay as the player said them; their order is WAIT ('don't shoot' HOLD_FIRE, 'don't move' HOLD_POSITION). A negation followed by an order is the two: 'don't jump down, come closer' -> 'Don't jump down.', 'Come closer to me.'.

11. The new orders split and complete like the others: 'go find ammo and then get in the car' -> 'Go find ammo.', 'Get in the car.' (MOVE_TO, GET_IN); 'get out and grab a rifle' -> 'Get out of the car.', 'Grab a rifle.' (GET_OUT, MOVE_TO); 'wait here' stays 'wait here' (HOLD_POSITION). What the recognizer made of a word is kept as heard ('go find armor' stays 'go find armor': the place matcher knows 'armor' is ammo; 'breach on my goal' stays as it is: the timing rule knows 'goal').
